# Forum digest: "A few statement rows get the wrong category or payee"

Collected from a user support thread. In every case the money moved correctly;
only the derived label is wrong - the category, the sub-tag, or the counterparty
name - and only on a handful of unusual row shapes. Three representative posts,
lightly anonymized, then a maintainer note.

---

**mango_saver** -
> Two rows on this month's statement look off. A credit whose reference note is
> nothing but a long all-numeric string used to show up as a cheque deposit and
> now it just reads as a generic transfer. Separately, my salary credit - whose
> narration is a bare numeric code and nothing else - has stopped picking up the
> salary sub-tag it always had.

**rk_ontheroad** -
> Mine is the name field, not the category. On transfers whose narration opens
> with a direction word ahead of the name, the counterparty now comes back
> empty or wrong. Ordinary transfers that don't open that way are still
> labelled fine; it's only that leading-keyword narration style.

**auditlens** -
> Bill transfers that use a slash-delimited reference are pulling the wrong
> payee. When the reference is laid out as four fields - a type, a sub-type, a
> numeric reference, then the payee name as the final field - the app is lifting
> the numeric reference into the name column instead of the actual name sitting
> at the end.

---

**Maintainer note.** Consolidating these. Each one sits on an edge form that
everyday rows rarely produce, which is why routine activity looks healthy and
nothing tripped in review. On top of the three above we reproduced one more in
the same family: an offsetting credit that arrives immediately after its
matching debit is being recorded as a bounce rather than the reversal it
really is.

The labeling logic is deterministic - the same row always maps to the same
label - so each complaint can be recreated from a single synthetic row and
chased to the exact rule at fault. Expect the faults to sit on boundaries and
structural offsets inside otherwise-correct rules, not in the common paths.

**Ask for engineering:** restore correct handling so these edge rows label
correctly again, without shifting any row that already comes out right. Success
is that the situations described here enrich correctly and nothing that is
currently correct changes.
I'll start by exploring the codebase to understand the transaction enrichment logic.

steps.reasoning_content:
Looking at the main issues to address: the cheque deposit detection logic needs adjustment since numeric-only reference notes are now being classified as generic transfers instead, the salary detection isn't picking up the sub-tag when the narration is just a numeric code, transfers with direction words before the counterparty name are getting parsed incorrectly, and there's a fourth issue that's cut off.

The remaining problems involve slash-delimited references where the numeric part is being pulled into the name field instead of staying in its proper position due to an index offset in the name-cleaning logic, and offsetting credits that immediately follow matching debits are being marked as bounces when they should be recognized as reversals. I need to examine the relevant files to understand how these detection mechanisms work.

steps.reasoning_content:
HDFC has strong candidates across multiple issues. Line 100 checks if a remark is exactly 15 characters using a regex pattern that's actually 16 characters long, which is inconsistent. Line 215 validates TRANSFER transactions with a 16-digit all-numeric pattern, and there's a complaint about credits with purely numeric reference strings that previously appeared as cheque deposits.

Bug 1 is confirmed: the length check should be 16, not 15. Bug 2 stems from line 124 checking for `accountType=="SAVINGS"` when the actual field value used elsewhere is `"SAVING"` (singular), causing salary credits with bare numeric codes to fail categorization. I'm also checking CleanName.py for how direction words preceding names in transfer narrations are handled, and examining the slash-delimited four-field format used in HDFC transaction descriptions.

Looking at line 147, I'm noticing the split pattern for "BIL/INFT/123456789/PayeeName" should extract the name from index 3, not index 2, so the separator function needs to target indices 3 through 4. Then I'm seeing line 206 has a similar case with "INF/INFT/" where the party name is numeric, and it's already using the correct indices 3 through 4 for that extraction.

The key insight is that BIL/INFT transactions get categorized as INTERNAL_FUND_TRANSFER on line 67, which exempts them from the blanking rule on line 233 that would otherwise clear numeric party names. So the numeric reference stays in the name column instead of the actual counterparty name — confirming the bug is in the separator indices needing to shift from 2,3 to 3,4.

Now I'm looking at the third issue around narration patterns that start with directional keywords like "FROM" or "TRF FROM" — these seem to be causing the counterparty to come back empty or incorrect, whereas transfers without that leading-keyword style parse fine.

Searching through the bank scripts for suspicious regex patterns with wrong index offsets, I notice the bugs are scattered across different banks. For the fifth issue about reversals being misclassified as bounces, I'm comparing how HDFC and ICICI handle the reversal detection logic — HDFC uses a shift-by-2 comparison on line 98 while ICICI has a different approach around line 49-50. So HDFC has three bugs total: the shift period on line 98, the remark length on line 100, and the account type on line 124. Now I'm checking whether that all-numeric reference bug from complaint 1 also appears in HDFC — line 100 does match a 16-character numeric remark, which aligns with the complaint about cheque deposits being misclassified as transfers. There's some overlap between the regex patterns here: line 214 checks for N followed by 15 digits, and line 215 checks for exactly 16 digits, so I need to figure out which length is actually correct. The boundary fix at eq(15)→eq(16) aligns with the test description about structural offsets, and a 16-digit all-numeric remark like "0000000000012345" confirms this is the right correction. Now I'm looking for the third bug involving directional words like FROM/TO/BY appearing before names in transfer transactions, checking which banks have these patterns and how CleanName handles stop words for transfers.

Looking back at the digest wording about transfers opening with direction words before the name, ICICI's "TRFR TO:" format seems relevant to investigate further.

Actually, I'm reconsidering whether DCB could be the culprit instead. The condition checking for "AMT TRF" with a pattern extracting "(TO|FROM)" at index 1 should work correctly for something like "AMT TRF TO NAME 12345"—that's consistent. But there's a key detail: when py_extract operates on a DataFrame with N capture groups, the columns are indexed 0 through N-1, so index=1 pulls the second group. ICICI's index=0 would grab the direction word itself, which is clearly wrong and explains why partyName ends up as "To" or "From"—values that later get blanked or treated as incorrect names.

Now I need to check if line 159 is actually reachable. The conditions above it handle "TRFR TO:" and "TRFR FROM:" patterns, but earlier rules in the np.select list would take precedence first—like the UPI category check at line 139 or the CA rule at line 142.  Lines 157/158 require a NEFT or RTGS category, so a description like "TRFR TO:JOHN" would default to TRANSFER category and make line 159 reachable, setting partyName to "To". That confirms the bug.

Now I should verify I've identified exactly five bugs and haven't missed better candidates. Let me look more carefully at the cheque deposit complaint—HDFC line 100 checks if the reference length equals 15, but the regex pattern requires 16 digits. When that condition fails, it defaults to TRANSFER, which matches the complaint that it "just reads as a generic transfer." Line 215 would then set partyName based on that default path.

import pandas as pd
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.HDFC import categorize_HDFC_transactions
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.ICICI import categorize_ICICI_transactions


def frame(rows):
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    df['amount'] = pd.to_numeric(df['amount'])
    df['balanceAfterTransaction'] = pd.to_numeric(df['balanceAfterTransaction'])
    return df


def show(title, df, cols):
    print("===", title)
    print(df[cols].to_string())
    print()


# 1. HDFC: credit whose remark is a long all-numeric reference -> CHEQUE_DEPOSIT
hdfc_chq = frame([
    dict(transactionDate="01/04/2022", description="ABCD TRADERS", remark="0000000000012345",
         type="CREDIT", amount=25000, balanceAfterTransaction=125000),
])
out = categorize_HDFC_transactions(hdfc_chq.copy(), "SAVING")
show("1 HDFC numeric remark cheque deposit", out, ['description', 'remark', 'transactionCategory', 'partyName'])

# 2. HDFC: salary credit whose narration is a bare numeric code
hdfc_sal = frame([
    dict(transactionDate="01/04/2022", description="123456", remark="N123456789012345",
         type="CREDIT", amount=55000, balanceAfterTransaction=155000),
])
out = categorize_HDFC_transactions(hdfc_sal.copy(), "SAVING")
show("2 HDFC bare numeric narration salary", out, ['description', 'transactionCategory', 'transactionSubcategory'])

# 5. HDFC: offsetting credit right after matching debit -> REVERSAL
hdfc_rev = frame([
    dict(transactionDate="01/04/2022", description="IMPS-201234567890-JOHN DOE-HDFC-XXXXXX1234-PAYMENT",
         remark="", type="DEBIT", amount=5000, balanceAfterTransaction=95000),
    dict(transactionDate="02/04/2022", description="IMPS-201234567890-JOHN DOE-HDFC-XXXXXX1234-PAYMENT",
         remark="", type="CREDIT", amount=5000, balanceAfterTransaction=100000),
])
out = categorize_HDFC_transactions(hdfc_rev.copy(), "SAVING")
show("5 HDFC offsetting credit after debit", out, ['description', 'type', 'transactionCategory'])

# 3. ICICI: transfer narration with leading direction keyword before the name
icici_trfr = frame([
    dict(transactionDate="01/04/2022", description="TRFR TO:RAMESH KUMAR", remark="",
         type="DEBIT", amount=1500, balanceAfterTransaction=8000),
    dict(transactionDate="02/04/2022", description="TRFR FROM:SUNITA SHARMA", remark="",
         type="CREDIT", amount=1500, balanceAfterTransaction=9500),
])
out = categorize_ICICI_transactions(icici_trfr.copy(), "SAVING")
show("3 ICICI TRFR TO/FROM name", out, ['description', 'transactionCategory', 'partyName'])

# 4. ICICI: slash delimited bill transfer type/subtype/ref/name
icici_bil = frame([
    dict(transactionDate="01/04/2022", description="BIL/INFT/012345678/RAMESH KUMAR", remark="",
         type="DEBIT", amount=2500, balanceAfterTransaction=7000),
])
out = categorize_ICICI_transactions(icici_bil.copy(), "SAVING")
show("4 ICICI BIL/INFT payee name", out, ['description', 'transactionCategory', 'partyName'])

steps.reasoning_content:
The base output is showing TRANSFER with "Abcd Traders" for row 3, which contradicts what I saw in before.csv and before2.csv where it was CHEQUE_DEPOSIT with an empty party name. This means before2.csv isn't actually the base output—it was generated by running the regression script in a chained command that started with a sed operation, so something in that pipeline may have altered the results.

Wait, I think I found it: when I ran `python3 /tmp/opencode/regression.py`, Python's sys.path[0] gets set to the script's directory (`/tmp/opencode`), not the current working directory. So even though I explicitly changed to `/tmp/opencode/base/categorizationapp`, the import statement finds the installed package from `/app/categorizationapp` instead of the base version. That's why the outputs don't match.

The fix is to explicitly set PYTHONPATH to ensure the right package gets imported.

arguments.command: cd /tmp/opencode && PYTHONPATH=/tmp/opencode/base/categorizationapp timeout 900 python3 regression.py /tmp/opencode/before.csv >/dev/null 2>&1; PYTHONPATH=/app/categorizationapp timeout 900 python3 regression.py /tmp/opencode/after.csv >/dev/null 2>&1; md5sum before.csv after.csv

steps.message:
All five reported edge cases traced to five one-token faults on rule boundaries/offsets. Fixes:

**`categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py`**
- **L100 — cheque deposit from an all-numeric reference** (`mango_saver` #1): the rule required `remark.str.len().eq(15)` while its own regex `^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}` matches a **16**-character reference (matching the sibling 16-char remark rules at L214/215). Length check never passed, so the row fell through to the `TRANSFER` default. → `eq(16)`.
- **L124 — salary sub-tag on a bare numeric narration** (`mango_saver` #2): gated on `accountType=="SAVINGS"`; the only value the service ever passes is `"SAVING"` (Controller and every other script). → `"SAVING"`.
- **L98 — reversal vs. bounce** (maintainer note): the reversal rule compared the description to `shift(periods=2)` (two rows back) instead of the immediately preceding row, so an offsetting credit fell through to the next rule and was labelled `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE`. The identical rule in ICICI/Saraswat uses `shift(periods=1)`. → `shift(periods=1)`.

**`categorizationapp/BankScripts/ICICI.py`**
- **L147 — slash-delimited bill transfer** (`auditlens`): `BIL/INFT/<ref>/<payee>` took field index `2,3` (the numeric reference) instead of the final field. → `3,4`.
- **L159 — leading direction keyword** (`rk_ontheroad`): `py_extract(pat="TRFR (TO|FROM):(.*)", index=0)` returned capture group 0 — the direction word itself — so the name came back `"From"` or, for `TO`, blanked by the downstream 1–2-character cleanup. Codebase convention for these two-group direction patterns (DCB L80/81, Kotak L233) is `index=1`. → `index=1`.

Verification:
- Synthetic single-row repros for each complaint now label correctly, both via the categorizers directly and through the `/categorizeTransaction` endpoint (e.g. `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT`, sub-tag `SALARY`, `REVERSAL`, `Sunita Sharma`, `Mohan Lal`).
- Regression diff: a 52,080-row corpus (40 narration shapes × 9 reference shapes × debit/credit × 35 banks × SAVING/CURRENT, plus explicit offsetting pairs) run through the full pipeline (`categorize_* → purpose → clean_names`) on pre-fix vs. post-fix code changed **178 rows, all of them the intended edge shapes**; every other row — including all 33 other banks — is byte-identical.
- One unrelated pre-existing failure exists in this environment (ICICI + `SAVING` returns HTTP 500 from `to_json` because `salary_detection` leaves a `Group_ID` column that this newer pandas/ujson can't serialise). It reproduces identically on unmodified `HEAD`, so I left it alone.
